summary: DOSBox-X 2026.05.02 Vga save blob layout for Wiz6 mode-0x0D (320x200 EGA 16-color). VRAM at blob offset 0x80000, 4-plane interleaved (plane = byte-index % 4 within each 4-byte group). Two contamination regions must be zeroed during decode: (1) blob[0x0810E0..0x08171F] = rows 27-36 (DOSBox-X internal state: timer counters, config pointers, EGA attribute-controller lookup tables); (2) blob[0x82F70..0x838CE] = rows 75-90 (VGA hardware register state dump). Both are confirmed non-game-VRAM via cross-save invariance analysis across all 13 saves. After both masks: save 1 decodes with 0 noisy pixels in rows 8-48 and 100% top-third black.

findings.claim: VGA VRAM (vga.mem.linear) starts at blob offset 0x80000 in every captured save state.

evidence.vram_total_size: 0x44F48 bytes = 282440 bytes (standard 256KB VRAM + 0x4F48 bytes of DOSBox-X internal tables at end)
evidence.validation: Decoding as interleaved-plane VRAM with vram_start=0x80000 produces plausible Wiz6 game screens (black 84-85%, dark-gray 8-18%, full-width dark bars present in save 1 with full-screen window chrome).
evidence.alternative_tested: vram_start=0x84800 gave 50.1% black / 35.3% dark-gray (too dark — wrong).
evidence.alternative_tested_2: Planar layout (separate 64KB planes at 0x00000/0x10000/0x20000/0x30000) gave 99.2% black (entirely empty — wrong).

findings.claim: VGA VRAM is stored as 4-plane interleaved: for VGA address A and plane P, the byte is at blob[0x80000 + A*4 + P].

evidence.observable: Non-zero bytes in the blob appear at offsets that are multiples of 4 (e.g., +0x0003, +0x0007, +0x000b = plane 3 bytes only), consistent with plane-3-only pixels (EGA color 8 = dark gray window background).
evidence.verified_by: Decoding with interleaved formula produces structured image; planar layout produces blank image.

findings.claim: CRTC display-start address = 0 (registers 0x0C/0x0D both = 0x00) in save 1. No page flipping active at this game state.

evidence.vde_calculation: CRTC[0x12]=0x8F, overflow bit8=1, bit9=0 → VDE=0x18F=399 → 400 scanlines (double-scanned 200 logical rows)

findings.claim: CRTC offset register (reg 0x13) = 0x14 = 20 → row stride = 40 bytes per row per plane. Correct for 320-pixel-wide mode 0x0D.
DAC palette is at blob offset 0x82FE9, 768 bytes (256 entries × 3 channels × 6-bit values).

evidence.fast_path_verified: 0x82FE9 passes the all-bytes-≤0x3F heuristic plus entry-0=black and entry-15=bright constraints.
evidence.note: The DAC region falls within the VGA state-dump block (blob[0x82F70..0x838CE]) which overlaps with VRAM rows 75-90. See finding 'vga-state-dump-contamination'.

findings.claim: Direct EGA_DEFAULT[pixel_index] lookup produces correct RGB without going through the Attribute Controller → DAC path.

evidence.cross_ref: docs/re/findings/state4-runtime-palette.json: live VGA DAC across all saves = BIOS-default EGA palette, distance 0.
evidence.explanation: The AC registers perform a non-identity remapping, but dosbox_identify_palette confirmed the rendered pixel colors match EGA_DEFAULT exactly (distance 0). The 16 composed colors (pixel_index → AC[idx] → DAC[AC[idx]] → RGB) are identical to EGA_DEFAULT. Render against EGA_DEFAULT and the colors will match the engine framebuffer.
evidence.note: The AC register at blob 0x82FC2 is within the VGA state-dump block (rows 75-90 area) but reading AC registers for palette identification (not VRAM decode) is correct — these are hardware config, not display pixels.

findings.claim: DOSBox-X 2026.05.02 stores internal state (timer counters, config pointers, EGA attribute-controller lookup tables) at VGA addresses 0x0438–0x05C7, which maps to display rows 27–36 (blob[0x0810E0..0x08171F]). These bytes are NOT game-drawn VRAM — they must be zeroed during decode.

evidence.method: cross-save invariance analysis across all 13 saves
evidence.invariant_vga_addresses: 15 VGA addresses in rows 27-28 are byte-for-byte identical in all 13 saves (DOSBox-X internal pointers/config; e.g. VGA 0x0460 = planes 80,3D,02,68 = a 32-bit pointer value)
evidence.variant_vga_addresses: 4 VGA addresses in row 27 vary per save (timer/counter bytes: e.g. VGA 0x0455 has plane3 values F4,F6,A4,53,02,B1,60... cycling each save)
evidence.save1_extra: Save 1 has 94 additional non-zero VGA addresses in rows 28-36 (EGA attribute-controller lookup tables: 0x55/0xFF/0xAA patterns) serialized by DOSBox-X during save; saves 2-13 have zeroes there
evidence.total_contaminated_save1: 113 VGA addresses out of the 0x044B-0x05BA range
evidence.total_contaminated_saves2_13: 19 VGA addresses per save (the invariant subset)
evidence.fix: In decodeVgaScreen(): if blobBase >= DOSBOX_INTERNAL_BLOB_START (0x0810E0) and blobBase <= DOSBOX_INTERNAL_BLOB_END (0x08171F), treat pixel as index 0 (black)
evidence.actual_game_vram: All 13 saves have zero game VRAM at rows 27-36 (black top-window interior). After masking, rows 8-48 have 0 non-black/non-gray pixels.

findings.claim: DOSBox-X 2026.05.02 serializes VGA hardware register state (CRTC, sequencer, attribute controller, GFX controller, DAC palette, lookup tables) into blob[0x82F70..0x838CE], which overlaps with screen rows 75-90 in the interleaved VRAM mapping. These bytes must be treated as zero (= black, pixel-index 0) during VRAM decode.

evidence.affected_rows: 75-90 (16 rows × 160 bytes = 2560 byte region in interleaved VRAM)
evidence.invariance_proof: Bytes within this range are identical (or near-identical with ≤4 bytes variation) across all 13 captured save states. Specifically: rows 77, 84-89 are byte-for-byte identical; rows 75-76, 90 have ≤4 bytes varying. In contrast, real game VRAM at adjacent rows varies dramatically between saves (different characters, different screens).
evidence.identification: The data matches known VGA register values (CRTC: 2D 27 28 90 2B 80 BF 1F 00 C0...; AC palette: 17 11 15 14 16 12 13 10 07 01 05 04 06 02 03 00; DAC: 768 bytes of 6-bit RGB values starting at 0x82FE9). The alternating 0x55/0xAA/0xFF pattern in rows 85-90 matches the EGA default lookup table.
evidence.actual_vram_content: The game VRAM at those VGA addresses is all-zero (black window interior). The state dump overwrites it during DOSBox-X serialization.
evidence.fix_applied: In decodeVgaScreen(): if blobBase >= VGA_STATE_BLOB_START (0x82F70) and blobBase <= VGA_STATE_BLOB_END (0x838CE), treat pixel as index 0 (black).

decode_parameters.palette: EGA_DEFAULT (direct pixel_index → RGB, no AC stage needed)
decode_parameters.contamination_region_1: blob[0x0810E0..0x08171F] (rows 27-36) — DOSBox-X internal state, treat as pixel 0 (black)
decode_parameters.contamination_region_2: blob[0x82F70..0x838CE] (rows 75-90) — VGA register state dump, treat as pixel 0 (black)

before_fix_rows_27_36.note: Before the rows-27-36 mask: save 1 had 709 noisy pixels in rows 8-48 from DOSBox-X internal state (EGA lookup tables + timer data serialized at VGA addr 0x044B-0x05BA). Saves 2-13 each had 45 noisy pixels from the 19 invariant VGA addresses. All now zero after adding DOSBOX_INTERNAL_BLOB mask.

validation_save1.saves_all_pass: all 13 saves decode with 0 top-window noisy pixels and structural check PASS
